# Sirach Chapter 49 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 49 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 49 is brief (16 verses) but structurally complex. After Josiah (vv. 1–3) comes a summary judgment on the kings (vv. 4–6), then Jeremiah and the destruction (vv. 6–7), Ezekiel (v. 8), Job (v. 9), the Twelve Prophets (v. 10), Zerubbabel and Jeshua (vv. 11–12), Nehemiah (v. 13). The chapter then closes with a stunning reversal: Enoch, Joseph, Shem, Seth, and Adam (vv. 14–16) — a return to the very beginning, with Adam as the climax. The structure mirrors the opening of ch. 44.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 1: The incense simile for Josiah is one of the most beautiful in the book. "Prepared by the work of the perfumer" vs. "skillfully prepared" — SOPHIA preserves the craftsman reference.
- v. 7: "Jeremiah" is not named in the Greek (the pronoun refers back to v. 6). PNEUMA supplies the name for clarity; SOPHIA follows this.
- v. 8: "chariot of the cherubim" — the merkavah vision of Ezekiel 1. Preserve "chariot" (Greek harma).
- v. 9: "he also mentioned Job" — the allusion to Ezek. 14:14,20 where God names Noah, Daniel, and Job. The text says Ezekiel "mentioned" (emnēsthē) Job.
- v. 10: "twelve prophets" — the Book of the Twelve (minor prophets). "Spring up/sprout" from v. 12 of ch. 46 (bones sprouting) — SOPHIA maintains the botanical metaphor.
- v. 16: The closing verse on Adam is the climax of the entire Praise of the Ancestors. "Above every living thing was Adam in his creation" — this must be the final, ringing statement of primordial human glory before the shift to Simon II in ch. 50.

---

**49:1** The memory of Josiah is like a blending of incense, prepared by the work of the perfumer; it is sweet as honey in every mouth, and like music at a banquet of wine.

**49:2** He did what was right in the conversion of the people and took away the abominations of lawlessness.

**49:3** He set his heart upon the Lord; in days of lawlessness he confirmed piety.

**49:4** Apart from David and Hezekiah and Josiah, all committed great offenses, for they forsook the law of the Most High — the kings of Judah failed to the very last.

**49:5** So they gave their power to others and their glory to a foreign nation,

**49:6** who set fire to the chosen city of the sanctuary and made its streets desolate — as Jeremiah had foretold.

**49:7** For they had mistreated him, who was consecrated as a prophet from the womb, to pull up and to tear down and to destroy, and likewise to build and to plant.

**49:8** It was Ezekiel who saw the vision of glory which God showed him above the chariot of the cherubim.

**49:9** For he also mentioned Job, who held fast to all the paths of righteousness.

**49:10** And may the bones of the twelve prophets sprout anew from where they lie! For they comforted the people of Jacob and rescued them with confident hope.

**49:11** How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He too was like a signet ring on the right hand.

**49:12** So also was Jeshua son of Jozadak; in their day they built the house and raised up the holy temple of the Lord, destined for everlasting glory.

**49:13** Also the memory of Nehemiah is great; he rebuilt for us the walls that had fallen, and set up gates and bars, and restored our ruined houses.

**49:14** No one like Enoch has ever been created on earth, for he was taken up from the earth.

**49:15** Nor was any man like Joseph, who was born; and his body was kept watch over.

**49:16** Shem and Seth were honored among men, but above every living thing in creation was Adam.
